findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||
findings.body: The check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. A team admin who is not an owner (the common case for delegated management) will fail this check even though the intent is clearly 'admin OR owner'. Use `||` so team admins can add guests to their team's bookings.

findings.title: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests via the API
findings.body: The handler authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches one of the booking's attendees (`isAttendee`). The UI only exposes this action to the organizer, but the tRPC mutation is callable by any authenticated attendee, letting an external guest with a cal.com account add unlimited arbitrary email addresses to someone else's booking (spam vector, data exposure of the event/ICS to arbitrary addresses). There is also no rate limit and no cap on the number of guests per request. Authorization should be restricted to the organizer / team admin.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the calling user. If the caller is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), the calendar update (`updateCalendarAttendees`) runs against the caller's calendar/credential set, not the booking owner's, so the guest update will be applied to the wrong calendar or fail. The organizer's credentials (already included in the booking query via `user.credentials`) should be used.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist email checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: Blacklist entries are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but then compared with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` using the raw guest string, so `User@Example.com` bypasses a blacklisted `user@example.com`. Similarly `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so a guest already on the booking with different casing is re-added as a duplicate attendee row (and receives duplicate emails). Both the guest input and stored emails should be normalized (e.g. lowercased) before comparison.

findings.title: Email failure swallowed and wrong guests list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails
findings.body: Two problems: (1) the catch block only logs `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` without the error object, so failures are undiagnosable and silently ignored; (2) `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw input `guests` rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so emails that were skipped (already attendees or blacklisted) are still treated as 'new' in email-manager's `newGuests.includes(...)` check (case-sensitively too), causing an existing attendee who was also submitted again to receive a full 'scheduled' email instead of the add-guests email.

findings.title: Error toast interpolates translation of a translation key that may not exist
findings.body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` assumes `err.message` is a translation key present in common.json. TRPC errors thrown from other layers (e.g. Prisma or calendar update failures) return raw English messages or keys like `booking_not_found` that are not guaranteed to exist, producing a toast like `BAD_REQUEST: booking_not_found` untranslated. Also, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never trigger since the template string is always non-empty.

findings.title: Add-guests action offered for cancelled/past/unconfirmed bookings
findings.body: The `add_members` entry is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`, which is included in `bookedActions` for past and even cancelled bookings (cancel filter only removes the cancel action). Adding guests to a cancelled or already-ended booking still fires calendar updates and sends 'new guests added' confirmation emails for an event that no longer happens. The action should be gated on `!isCancelled` and the booking being in the future.

findings.title: No tests for the addGuests handler
findings.body: The new mutation contains non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / team admin / attendee), dedup, blacklisting, and a calendar side effect, but the PR adds no integration or unit tests. The `&&` vs `||` admin bug (see separate finding) is exactly the kind of regression a permission test would have caught. At minimum, tests for the forbidden path, the duplicate-guest path, and the blacklist path should be added before merge.
